alerts.title: TDF contraindicated with eGFR <60
alerts.message: Guidelines state TDF is contraindicated when GFR <60 mL/min. Patient's eGFR is 52 mL/min/1.73m² (CKD-EPI), below the 60 mL/min threshold. TDF has been prescribed for 3 years. The patient has no diabetes or hypertension, and urinalysis shows protein 1+, which may indicate TDF-related renal tubular damage. However, other causes of CKD should be excluded. TDF should be discontinued and replaced with TAF, which guidelines state is preferred over TDF.

evidence.recommended_action: Discontinue TDF immediately and switch to TAF-based regimen. Investigate non-drug causes of renal impairment. Refer to nephrology if indicated.

alerts.title: Rising creatinine trend over 5 years
alerts.message: Guidelines require annual serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring for patients on TDF. Patient's creatinine has progressively risen from 0.9 (2020) to 1.4 mg/dL (2026), with eGFR declining to 52 mL/min/1.73m². This steady worsening over 5 years signals ongoing renal injury even if individual values were previously within range. Protein 1+ on urinalysis further supports renal tubular dysfunction. TDF nephrotoxicity is a likely contributor given the temporal relationship with 3 years of TDF use. Non-drug causes should also be evaluated.

evidence.recommended_action: Switch from TDF to TAF. Conduct comprehensive renal assessment including renal ultrasound and urine protein-to-creatinine ratio.

alerts.title: TDF toxicity symptoms present
alerts.message: Guidelines list exhaustion, extreme fatigue, muscle cramps, and headache as presenting signs of TDF toxicity including lactic acidosis and Fanconi syndrome. Patient reports mild fatigue over 2 months. While she attributes this to work schedule, TDF has been used for 3 years and renal function is declining with proteinuria, making TDF toxicity a plausible contributor. Against drug attribution: fatigue is non-specific and her busy schedule provides an alternative explanation. No muscle cramps or headache are reported. Given eGFR 52, TDF should be discontinued regardless.

evidence.recommended_action: Evaluate for TDF toxicity including LFTs, RFTs, and serum lactate. Discontinue TDF and switch to TAF given renal impairment.

alerts.title: No clinician plan documented
alerts.message: Guidelines require use of a screening tool to identify developing signs and symptoms in patients on ART, and TDF-specific annual creatinine and eGFR monitoring. No assessment or plan was documented for this visit despite abnormal eGFR (52), proteinuria, rising creatinine trend, and patient-reported fatigue. Required actions include renal evaluation, TDF discontinuation per contraindication criteria, and symptom screening. The absence of a plan represents a guideline deviation given the clear abnormalities present.

evidence.recommended_action: Document assessment addressing eGFR 52, proteinuria, and fatigue. Plan TDF discontinuation, renal workup, and ART regimen modification.
